title: SpaceX's $75 Billion IPO Makes Musk the First Trillionaire. Indian Investors Are Scrambling to Get In.
excerpt: Indian investment platforms report 'unprecedented' traffic as retail investors chase the world's largest stock offering through LRS and US-listed intermediaries.
body:
SpaceX opened for trading on the Nasdaq on Friday at $150 a share, 11 per cent above its $135 IPO price, before surging to $176 at midday and settling at $160.95 — a 19 per cent first-day pop that valued the company at $2.1 trillion. It is now the sixth-largest public company in the United States, worth more than Tesla, the electric vehicle maker also run by its founder and CEO Elon Musk.

The listing raised $75 billion — more than double the previous IPO record — and instantly pushed Musk's net worth past $1.1 trillion, making him the first person in history to cross the trillionaire threshold. Forbes estimates his SpaceX holdings alone are worth roughly $866 billion. Around 4,400 current and former SpaceX employees became millionaires overnight.

## Indian Platforms Report Record Traffic

The ripple effects reached India within hours. Vested Finance, a platform that allows Indian residents to invest in US equities under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme, said it had already made the SpaceX ticker live and was seeing "unprecedented" search traffic. "Marquee IPOs always lead to traction, but this has been unlike anything we've seen," said Viram Shah, founder and CEO of Vested Finance.

Borderless, another cross-border investing platform, estimated that if the IPO allocation had been open to Indian retail investors, demand could have translated into $50–100 million in investments. Its founder Sitashwa Srivastava predicted that daily trading volume on the platform would more than double on the first post-listing trading day, driven largely by SpaceX-related interest.

Data from the Reserve Bank of India shows that remittances under LRS for investment in foreign equity and debt grew 56 per cent year-on-year to $2.7 billion in FY26 — a figure that is likely to accelerate as listings like SpaceX draw retail attention.

## Allocation Shortfalls and the Retail Rush

Not everyone who wanted in got in. On Reddit forums devoted to tracking allocations, investors reported requesting hundreds of shares and receiving ten, or none at all. The IPO was oversubscribed by four times, according to Bloomberg, meaning most institutional investors failed to secure full allocations and turned to the open market.

Musk had pledged in 2024 that if any of his private companies went public, retail investors — especially Tesla shareholders — would receive priority access. Robinhood reported "record-breaking" traffic on Friday following the listing.

Vanda Research, which tracks self-directed individual investors, said SpaceX was the single most actively purchased stock by retail investors within hours of the opening bell. The company leapfrogged Nvidia, which had held the top spot for much of 2026.

## The Indian Supply Chain Connection

Beyond portfolio interest, SpaceX's public listing has drawn attention to its Indian supply chain. INOX India, which holds a $21 million contract for cryogenic systems used in aerospace applications — reportedly linked to a leading US-based private space company — saw its shares surge 25 per cent in the month leading up to the listing. Investors are increasingly viewing the company as a proxy play on the broader space industry's expansion.

## What It Means for NRI Investors

For Indians living abroad, particularly in the United States, the listing is a straightforward equity purchase. For residents in India, the path runs through LRS-compliant platforms, with an annual $250,000 per-person remittance cap. Some investors are also looking at indirect exposure through funds like the Destiny Tech Fund (DXYZ), a publicly traded vehicle that holds pre-IPO SpaceX shares, available on select Indian global investing platforms.

The broader signal may be even more consequential. Anthropic and OpenAI are both preparing public offerings later this year. If SpaceX's debut is any indication — and Gavekal Research has cautioned that the market "may struggle to absorb a wave of mega-IPOs" — the appetite for US tech listings among Indian investors is not a passing phase. It is a structural shift, and the pipes for cross-border capital flow are only getting wider.

*Sources: Reuters, TechCrunch, The Hindu BusinessLine, Motley Fool, Associated Press*
